name: Decay
miniText: NetLogo Decay investigates how a constant individual decay probability creates a population half-life. Each still-radioactive nucleus receives an independent per-tick chance to decay, briefly flashes, and then remains stable; population and per-tick decay counts are recorded. Provides the foundational radioactive-transformation interpretation [1]. Relates measured alpha-particle ranges to characteristic transformation periods, a physical connection deliberately absent from the constant-probability baseline [2]. Clarifies continuous-time event sampling, exposing the distinction from a fixed-step Bernoulli decay probability [3]. The baseline omits daughter chains and isotope-specific interactions; a discrete probability p corresponds to an exponential survival rate through minus log of one minus p per time interval, rather than simply p at all step sizes. The simulation illustrates why an irregular sequence of individual events can produce an approximately exponential aggregate curve. Reproducing these patterns establishes rule fidelity, not empirical validation.
